## Simple explanation

A data pipeline is a repeatable sequence that takes data from one or more
sources, transforms it, and delivers it to a destination or application.

## Technical explanation

A pipeline may include ingestion, validation, cleaning, joining,
aggregation, feature generation, storage, and scheduling. Pipelines can
run in batches or process streams continuously. Reliable pipelines define
schemas, handle failures, track lineage, and make retries safe.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Models depend on consistent inputs for training, evaluation, and serving.
Pipelines help make data preparation reproducible and expose failures
before invalid or stale data reaches a model.

## How it works

An orchestrator or streaming system runs pipeline stages in dependency
order. Each stage reads inputs, performs a transformation, and writes
outputs. Quality checks, logs, metrics, and version information help
operators detect and diagnose problems.

## Practical example

A nightly pipeline can ingest labeled images, check file integrity and
class labels, create a versioned dataset manifest, and make the result
available for training.

## Common misconceptions

- A pipeline that completes successfully may still produce incorrect data.
- Pipelines need monitoring and recovery strategies, not just scheduled
  execution.
- A pipeline is not necessarily a single linear script; it may be a
  dependency graph with branching and parallel work.
